newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia hybrid corn area hit by locusts - report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia hybrid corn area hit by locusts - report.

text.p: A key Indonesian corn-growing area in southern Sumatra has been hit by locusts, which have destroyed 45 hectares of high-yielding hybrid crops, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.
The regent of the North Lampung region, A. Gumbira, was quoted as saying that the locust attack also damaged 200 hectares in South and Central Lampung, apart from the 45 hectares in North Lampung.
Gumbira was quoted by the North Lampung regency public relations officer Thabrani Achmad as saying farmers were concerned by the attack by the millions of locusts.
He said the farmers sprayed their crops with pesticides but it had so far been ineffective.
Antara said 40,000 hectares in North Lampung have been earmarked to be planted with the hybrid strain that yields as much as four times the two tonnes per hectare produced by ordinary species.
The agency said about 2,000 hectares have been planted so far with the hybrid in North Lampung.
Indonesia is hoping to end corn imports by 1999 by planting some 50,000 hectares with the hybrid strain.

The U.S. embassy in Jakarta said in a report it expected Indonesia to import 1.1 million tonnes of corn in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) U.S. marketing year, compared with trade estimated at 900,000-1.0 million tonnes in the same 1995/96 period.
